tob-13145: Swami Vivekananda’s seven talks on Jnana Yoga — the yoga of knowing — teach the road of sifting the true Self from the world’s passing show. Given in America in the 1890s, they bore Vedanta’s boldest word: that each soul is godlike already. The talks crackle with the Swami’s fire.
tob-0045: The Pentagon Papers are the Defense Department’s secret history of the Vietnam War, leaked by Daniel Ellsberg in 1971. This first Gravel-edition volume spans the war’s roots and buildup. The leak’s printing — and the high-court fight it lit — changed American journalism.
tob-4145: Julius Jolly’s rendering of the Vishnu Smriti turns one of Hinduism’s great law-books — rules for life, rite, and kings’ duties. A Sacred Books of the East volume, it opened India’s law-lore to the West. Its rede lights up olden Indian fellowship. The text shows a whole world-order in small.
tob-4245: A. M. Reeves’s Wineland the Good tells of Iceland’s finding of America — the Vinland sagas in scholar’s dress. His work fastened the Norse farings in American minds. The book stays the classic tale of Leif Ericsson’s voyage. A landmark of Viking book-lore.
cia-0000107445: An April 1948 report on communist activities across the Levant. With the British Empire pulling back and new states emerging, Moscow saw openings throughout the Eastern Mediterranean. The document is a snapshot of the CIA in its infancy, already drawing the map of communist influence in the Middle East.
cia-0000108045: An August 1982 report on the 107th Mining Administration prison camp at Krasnoyarsk-26, a closed Soviet nuclear city. Prisoners dug and hauled in a place so secret it did not appear on maps. The document ties the camp system directly to the Soviet military-industrial complex — forced labor feeding the bomb program.
cia-0000112345: An April 1992 summary of Beijing-based newspapers for May 14, compiled by China's Xinhua news agency. Reading the other side's press was daily bread for analysts — what gets printed reveals what the state wants believed. The document is one day's harvest from that endless reading.
cia-0000117845: Volume I, the overview, of a June 1995 investigation report on Guatemala. The CIA was finally accounting for its role in Guatemala's dirty war — assets, knowledge, and complicity. The document marks a rare moment of institutional self-examination, decades after the events.
cia-0000119745: The Hungarian situation as of 2:00 AM Eastern time — the small-hours update in a crisis that never slept. Overnight reports bridged the gap between Washington's evenings and Budapest's mornings. The entry keeps the round-the-clock record unbroken.
cia-0000126945: A January 1989 terrorism review of international terrorist actions in Latin America during 1988. The year-end format tallied a year's bombings, kidnappings, and assassinations across the hemisphere. The document is the annual accounting of political violence — the region's bloody ledger.
cia-0000132245: Situation Report 562 on potential political developments — the truncated title withholds the specifics. Analysts were gaming out what came after the shooting stopped. The entry is the future, forecasted: the war's aftermath, anticipated in advance.
cia-0000132745: A 1960 study of opposition to Castro: former Batista men, former Castro men — the truncated title suggests more factions. The enemy of the revolution wore many faces. The document is the opposition, catalogued: the exiles, the defectors, the disillusioned.
cia-0000134245: Item 1 in a 1960 general series: the bloc expanding economic ties with Cuba. The checkbooks kept opening. The document is the expansion: the ties, multiplying.
cia-0000135945: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN requesting geological information on WSBURNT and surroundings — the archive's spelling says informaiton. Terrain mattered for the invasion. The document is the survey: the ground, studied.

cia-0000139045: An untitled 1945 document on Gerhart Eisler being identical with Hans Berger of the Daily Worker — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The unmasking. The document is the identity: the alias, exposed.
un-ga-res-a-69-45: Resolution A/69/45, adopted in 2014 during the 69th session. The modern Assembly, deciding. The designation is certain; the subject is in the text.
un-ga-res-45: UN General Assembly Resolution 45, from 1946. The first session's later acts. The entry is the record: the forty-fifth, numbered and dated.
un-sc-res-145: Security Council Resolution 145, adopted in 1960. The Congo year's Council deliberated. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
un-sc-res-245: Security Council Resolution 245, adopted in 1968. The Council deciding. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-445: Security Council Resolution 445, adopted in 1979 — aligned. The Council deciding. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-1345: Security Council Resolution 1345, cataloged with the year 1999 — the numbering suggests 2001, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1645: Security Council Resolution 1645, adopted in December 2005 — the Peacebuilding Commission resolution, creating the UN's new body to shepherd war-torn countries toward lasting peace. un-sc-res-1845: Security Council Resolution 1845, cataloged with the year 2003 — the numbering suggests 2008, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
cia-0000135745: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000135745. The Spanish documents of the invasion year. The entry is the language: the Spanish, primary.
cia-0000136645: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136645. The exiles' papers, held firm-dated. The entry is the holding: the papers, secured.
cia-0000136745: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136745. The brigade's voice in Spanish, preserved. The entry is the voice: the language, theirs.
plos-pone-0000045: A 2006 PLOS ONE paper: predator mimicry — metalmark moths mimic their jumping spider predators. The prey dresses as the hunter to survive. The paper is the mimicry: the moths, disguised as spiders.
luther-bible-1545: Luther's Biblia of 1545 — the last edition of Martin Luther's German Bible overseen by the reformer himself before his death. His vigorous, plain-spoken German didn't just spread the Reformation; it helped forge the modern German language. The Bible is the reformer's: the German, Luther's — the language, remade.
gregory-great-morals-on-job-vol-2-1845: The second volume of Gregory the Great's Morals on the Book of Job, in the 1845 translation — Parts III through IV of the pope's exhaustive meditation. The commentary marches on through Job's trials. The volume is the continuation: the meditation, unbroken.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d45: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, October 16, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 45. London answered. The message is the answer: the prime minister, writing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d145: The President to the ambassador in Turkey, Steinhardt, November 20, 1943 — Document 145. The White House wrote Ankara's envoy. The message is the envoy: Steinhardt, instructed.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d245: A log of the trip, November 11, 1943 — Document 245. The presidential journey, logged. The log is the journey: the trip, recorded.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d345: The minister in Egypt, Kirk, to the president's special assistant Hopkins — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 345. Cairo wrote the insider. The cable is the insider's: Kirk, to Hopkins.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d445: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 445. The editors' seam. The note is the seam: the narrative, stitched.
arxiv-2605-08745: Quantum physics permits contextuality, a strange effect in which a measurement's outcome depends on which other measurements are performed alongside it. Pritam Roy, Thansingh Jankawat, Ranendu Adhikary, and A. S. Majumdar show that imposing an exclusion condition — ruling certain outcomes out — reshapes how this contextuality appears in real experiments. The 2026 paper works out the mathematics of that reshaping.
arxiv-2605-08845: Particle-physics experiments produce data faster than most systems can swallow — any pause means lost collisions. Toma-Stefan Cezar, Marios Maroudas, and Dieter Horns describe a modular data-acquisition platform with zero dead time, processing the firehose in real time on GPUs. The 2026 paper is instrumentation research for high-throughput science.
arxiv-2605-09245: Tracking objects across many cameras usually demands painstaking calibration. Ruiqi Xian, Deep Patel, Iain Melvin, and colleagues go calibration-free with CalibFree: self-supervised view feature separation for multi-camera multi-object tracking. The 2026 paper frees camera networks from the calibration lab.
arxiv-2605-09345: Pruning neural networks hits a plateau — beyond some sparsity, everything degrades — and not all features prune equally. Guangqi Li and Yongxin Li map the selection plateau and a sparsity-dependent hierarchy of pruning features. The 2026 paper is a field guide to cutting models down.
arxiv-2605-09545: Koopman operator theory lifts nonlinear dynamics into infinite-dimensional linear spaces — but only if the data cooperates. Yue Wu provides diagnostic certificates of data quality and regression identifiability for Koopman identification. The 2026 paper checks whether your data truly deserves the method.
arxiv-2605-10045: Visual autoregressive models extrapolating to higher resolutions need stage-aware RoPE remapping — ExtraVAR. Feihong Yan, Shaoyu Liu, Haixuan Wang, and colleagues develop the technique. The 2026 paper is visual generation that scales up gracefully. It remaps positions cleverly for higher resolutions.
plos-pone-0003445: Neonatologists tested a drug to protect premature lungs in this 2008 rat study. Newborns breathing too much oxygen suffer stalled lung development and inflammation, a model for bronchopulmonary dysplasia. Blocking the enzyme phosphodiesterase 4 eased both the hyperoxia damage and the failure of air sacs to form, suggesting a possible therapy for fragile newborn lungs.
plos-pone-0003545: Toxicologists caught a plastic chemical sabotaging stress hormones in this 2008 study. Dibutyltin, a stabilizer in PVC plastics and a widespread pollutant, disrupted the glucocorticoid receptor and blocked the hormone's normal suppression of inflammatory signals. The result shows how an everyday industrial chemical can quietly scramble immune regulation.
plos-pone-0003645: In 2008, a team mapped where a hormone switch lands on DNA. The androgen receptor binds set spots across the genome, and the team sorted those spots by job, using marks like histone acetylation as clues. The map splits the receptor's landing sites into groups with different roles, most tied to prostate cancer growth.
plos-pone-0003745: In 2008, Skinner, Anway, and Savenkova showed a grandparent's exposure reaching the grandchild's brain. A chemical encountered during pregnancy reprogrammed gene activity in the brain across generations and shifted anxiety behavior. The work is early evidence that environmental exposures can echo through family lines.
plos-pone-0003845: Back in 2008, a group watched brains link sounds to actions. McNamara, Buccino, and Menz tracked the neural dynamics as volunteers learned sound-action associations. The study probes the motor roots of communication, where moving and meaning first meet.
plos-pone-0003945: In 2008, Kawakita, Sato, and Makino showed nicotine stunting young bones. The drug acted on growth-plate cartilage cells through the alpha-7 nicotinic receptor, slowing skeletal growth. The mechanism adds bone damage to smoking's toll on growing bodies.
plos-pone-0004045: In 2008, Wu and Sato studied the plumbing of a fruit-fly embryo's heart. They measured the mechanics of cardiac pumping in living Drosophila embryos. The tiny heart's fluid dynamics were mapped beat by careful beat. The fly embryo offers a simple window on heart function and failure.
plos-pone-0004145: In 2009, Guwatudde, Wabwire-Mangen, and Eller tracked HIV in rural Uganda for years. Infection rates ran relatively low but clearly threatened to rise. The cohort study pinned down local risk factors. The warning guides prevention before the curve bends up.
plos-pone-0004245: In 2009, a team probed the old violin secret. Mineral preservatives in Stradivari and Guarneri wood shaped their sound. Chemical treatment, not just craft, made the magic. The finding rewrites the Cremona legend anew. The chemistry may guide modern instrument makers.
plos-pone-0004345: In 2009, Atkinson, Morris, and Ferrin drew maps of protein kinship. Sequence similarity networks visualized relationships across diverse protein superfamilies. The network view tamed data floods. The tool helps biologists navigate sequence space. The method handles the flood of new sequences.
plos-pone-0358945: Brain aneurysms are often treated by filling them with tiny metal coils — but sometimes blood flow returns, a dangerous reopening called recanalization. This paper develops methods to measure and classify these reopened, coiled aneurysms from medical scans. The work moves toward an automatic tool that could flag risky cases for doctors faster and more consistently than the human eye alone.
plos-pone-0343345: Pouring money into digital tech doesn’t automatically make a heavy-industry firm greener. This paper studied how different ‘value embedding modes’ — the ways digital investment connects to core business values — shape ESG performance in energy-intensive companies. The lesson: how you digitize matters more than how much you spend.
plos-pone-0358545: A brain bleed can steal thinking as well as movement. This Taiwanese study mapped the clinical and brain-imaging features of intracerebral hemorrhage patients and linked them to early post-stroke cognition. The associations give doctors clues about which patients face the steepest cognitive losses — and where rehab should focus.
plos-pone-0326645: Children with special health care needs depend on policy — and policies differ wildly. This scoping review compared public health policies for these children across OECD countries and Brazil. The comparison exposes which systems serve vulnerable children best and where the gaps yawn.
plos-pone-0358445: Insulin does more than move sugar — it also triggers shedding of RAGE, an inflammation receptor, from blood vessel walls. This paper showed insulin drives this shedding via Rab14-dependent ADAM10 trafficking in human aortic endothelial cells. The mechanism links insulin signaling to vascular inflammation control.
plos-pone-0353745: Well-being in America isn’t evenly shared. This cross-sectional study used the Gallup National Health and Well-Being Index to describe well-being by race and ethnicity, education level, and urbanicity. The detailed breakdowns reveal exactly where the gaps are widest — and who is being left behind.
plos-pone-0358245: Tiny Romulea wildflowers of the Tyrrhenian region hide cryptic diversity invisible to the eye. This paper used molecular identification and diversity assessment to sort out these Iridaceae species. The DNA work clarifies which species are truly which — and which ones most urgently need protection.
plos-pone-0354445: Staying active may protect aging lungs in China. This CHARLS-based study examined associations between physical activity levels and chronic lung diseases in middle-aged and older Chinese adults. The associations add lung health to exercise’s long list of benefits — with nationally representative data behind it.
plos-pone-0357045: Connected vehicles must authenticate each other securely — without revealing who’s who. This chaotic map-based scheme provides efficient anonymous authentication and key agreement for vehicular ad-hoc networks (VANETs). The cryptography keeps cars talking safely while preserving driver privacy.
plos-pone-0357445: This entry is a correction notice, not a research finding. It amends the paper on altered stress and fear responses in the VPA rat model of autism, covering behavioral differences across tactile, nociceptive, and social contexts. The correction sets the published record straight.
plos-pone-0357145: Weight loss interventions change children’s metabolism in measurable ways. This study examined the effects on fat metabolism — including adipocytokines and metabolic enzymes — in children with simple obesity. The metabolic data help programs move beyond the scale toward genuine health.
plos-pone-0321345: Sterilizing cold-chain equipment and temperature-sensitive medical devices defeats most methods — heat destroys them. Chlorine dioxide gas sterilization solves the dilemma. This paper validated the approach for cold-chain and temperature-sensitive devices, keeping the cold chain both cold and sterile.
plos-pone-0356745: Preparing the body before prostate removal — prehabilitation — may improve recovery dramatically. This scoping review mapped prehabilitation models for patients undergoing radical prostatectomy. The review charts what preparation works, giving surgical teams a menu of evidence-based options.
plos-pone-0355545: Reverse-engineering the biochemical networks inside cells from data alone is a grand challenge. This paper proposed Bayesian model discovery for exactly that task. The Bayesian approach doesn’t just fit a network — it quantifies uncertainty about which network is right.
plos-pone-0355045: Vasa previa — fetal vessels crossing the birth canal — can kill babies in minutes if unrecognized. This paper published the study protocol for the first national vasa previa perinatal registry. The planned registry will finally give obstetricians population-scale data on this obstetric emergency.
plos-pone-0355845: India’s National Sickle Cell Elimination Mission needs universal screening to succeed. This paper argued for strengthening the mission through universal access to point-of-care screening tests. The policy case is clear: cheap, rapid tests in every clinic could find millions of carriers and patients now going undetected.
plos-pone-0355745: Reused poultry litter shapes chicks’ gut microbes and immunity from day one. This paper studied reused litter’s effect on early cecal microbiota succession and immune cell distribution in layer chickens. The findings help producers decide whether recycling litter builds resilience or spreads risk.
europmc-pmc2824145: Before running a big clinical trial, researchers test the waters with a pilot study. This 2010 tutorial explains the what, why, and how of pilot studies. The authors guide readers through designing small trials that answer feasibility questions. The paper became a go-to reference for researchers planning their first major study.
europmc-pmc2887145: Septic ICU patients need sedation, but the drug choice may shape survival. This 2010 analysis of the MENDS trial compares dexmedetomidine versus lorazepam for sepsis outcomes. The authors find the newer sedative linked to better results. Their finding nudged ICUs toward lighter, brain-friendlier sedation.
europmc-pmc2941545: Aging fat tissue turns traitor to the body. This 2010 review links fat tissue, aging, and cellular senescence. The authors show old fat spreads aging signals to neighbors. Their overview connects belly fat to body-wide decline. Clearing these worn-out cells is now a hot therapy hunt.
europmc-pmc2949645: Breast tumor staining needs objective scoring, not eyeballing. This 2010 paper offers ImmunoRatio, a free web app for measuring ER, PR, and Ki-67 in images. The authors' tool standardizes pathology reads. Their app aided diagnosis worldwide. Pathologists adopted it for routine second opinions.
europmc-pmc2955045: Retaking the same brain quiz lifts scores on its own. This 2010 study tracks healthy adults through repeat mental tests over time. The authors gauge the practice boost. Their work warns trial runners to expect it. Drug trials now build the effect into their math.
europmc-pmc2972245: Fat zebrafish get sick like fat mammals. This paper shows diet-induced obesity in zebrafish shares disease pathways with mammalian obesity. The authors validate a tiny model. Their work offers a fast screen for obesity drugs. A tank of fish beats a room of mice.
europmc-pmc3023445: Dengue type 3 swept the globe. This 2003 paper tracks one dengue strain's rise and worldwide march. The authors map its spread country by country. Their work warned health agencies. Mosquito control failed to halt the wave. The strain still sparks outbreaks today.
europmc-pmc3040745: A common virus may raise death risk. This 2011 paper links the widespread CMV virus to inflammation and higher US death rates. The authors' finding intrigues immunologists. Their work points to aging research. Half of adults carry the quiet passenger. The link needs proving, the authors caution.
europmc-pmc3044745: Brown fat hides in the obese too. This 2011 paper finds calorie-burning brown fat even in very obese people. The authors' scans reveal the furnace. Their work points to metabolic therapy. Cold snaps switch the furnace on. Drugs that stoke it are in trials.
europmc-pmc3049145: Partner violence got global data. This 2011 WHO study probes what drives partner violence against women across countries. The authors' vast data demands action. Their work shaped policy. Alcohol and male control topped the risk list. The study covered 15 sites in 10 countries.
europmc-pmc3087445: Lead and cadmium poison through oxidation. This 2011 review covers how the two metals spark oxidant damage and how to counter it. The authors survey harm and remedies. Their overview guides treatment. Antioxidants show promise as antidotes. Workers and kids face the worst exposure.
europmc-pmc6512245: CAR-T therapy - reprogramming a patient's own immune cells to hunt cancer - only works well when the engineered cells get strong internal "go" signals. Those signals come from costimulatory domains built into the receptor. This review compares the leading domain options, weighing how each affects cell growth, staying power, and tumor-killing ability, to guide the next generation of cancer treatments.
europmc-pmc6572845: ICU monitors stream vital signs by the second - a goldmine for machine learning if models can juggle many tasks at once. This paper benchmarks multitask learning on clinical time-series data: one model predicting several outcomes together. The tests show shared learning beats single-task models, pushing hospital AI toward the bedside.
europmc-pmc6602445: For twenty years, PSIPRED has been the go-to workbench for predicting protein structures from sequence alone. This paper describes the overhaul keeping it ready for the next twenty: refreshed methods, a modern interface, and the same free access. A bioinformatics institution gets its tune-up.
europmc-pmc6704245: The human cortex - seat of thought, language, and memory - builds itself through an elaborate developmental choreography. This research article reviews new insights into how the cerebral cortex forms: the cell migrations, layering, and wiring that assemble our most complex tissue. Understanding the build illuminates what can go wrong.
europmc-pmc6714445: Tumors recruit fibroblasts and turn them into bodyguards that blunt immune attack. This review makes the case for targeting cancer-associated fibroblasts with immunotherapy: strip away the stromal shield and T cells can reach their prey. The stroma, long ignored, becomes a bullseye.
europmc-pmc6722045: Childhood cancer is rare - but worldwide, rare adds up. Analyzing Global Burden of Disease 2017 data, this study estimates how many children and teens develop and die from cancer across the globe. The numbers expose stark inequities: survival depends heavily on where a child lives.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-45: A 2007 Government Accountability Office report on the Postal Service's fund-raising stamps — the semipostals whose surcharge supports causes like breast-cancer research. GAO examines how agencies distributed the proceeds and found reporting had improved. The report gives Congress a ledger on a small but beloved program where buying stamps doubles as charitable giving.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1045: Veterans' school benefits needed a better blueprint in 2007 — GAO's report says the VA's education-aid systems lacked guiding plans. The findings press for real planning behind the promises to former troops. A benefit is only as good as the machinery that delivers it.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-945: Medicare's private-plan audits were paper tigers in 2007 — GAO's report says the required checkups delivered little value. The findings question whether the watchdog's leash on Medicare Advantage was long enough to matter. Billions flowed to private insurers; the audits barely rippled the water.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-645: The FHA was losing its home-loan crown in 2007 — GAO's report ties the shrinking market share to product and process drift. The findings diagnose the fade of the New Deal-era lender. The report asks whether the agency could still matter in a market that had moved on.
gao-gaoreports-b-299545: Basic Concepts took its May 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict. The firm said the agency's award was unfair; the call tests the protest against the bid rulebook. Plain name, full process: every bidder, big or small, gets the same fair hearing in the protest system.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-745: The SEALs' mini-sub needed a contract that worked in 2007 — GAO's report says the advanced delivery system's success hinged on a sound buying strategy. The findings target the procurement plan. The report's warning: exotic hardware dies without boring-good contracting.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-445: Screening checked bags at LA and beyond cost real money in 2007 — GAO's report prices the TSA's baggage-system funding for the airports. The findings put hard numbers to the security. The report asks whether the big bill truly matched the threat.
gao-gaoreports-b-299145: Sikorsky and Lockheed Martin tripled their February 2007 protest — three case numbers, one helicopter fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles all three. The giants challenged the awards, and the call weighs each claim. Even the biggest names bow to bid law.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-245: The highway emergency fund was running on fumes in 2007, and GAO's report says the program needed reexamination for fiscal balance and sustainability. The findings demand the math. The report warns that the road rescue fund could not rescue itself. The potholes were not fixing themselves.
openalex-w7204924345: ADHD is showing up in more classrooms every year, and teachers are on the front line. This article studies how attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder appears in the school environment and what schools can do to handle it better. Rather than treating the condition as a discipline problem, the authors ask how teaching can adapt. Aimed at educators, it reframes ADHD as a classroom reality to understand, not a behavior to punish.
openalex-w7204188645: Children who survive brain tumors face a second battle: staying in school. This study follows survivors diagnosed in childhood and teens, tracing how cancer and its treatment shaped their school lives. The authors examine the educational support they got, or missed. Moving and important, it treats schooling as part of healing.
openalex-w7204094145: A phone app could watch over mother and baby together. This paper presents a prototype maternal-child health app built on scientific evidence, designed to predict pregnancy risks and guide full care for both. The authors describe the build and its promise for health services. Applied research where software meets the nursery.
openalex-w7152621645: AI that creates text and images is knocking on the clinic door. This comprehensive review covers generative AI in medicine: the core technologies, clinical uses, and paths to real deployment. The authors explained the principles before the promises. A big-picture guide to the hospital's AI future.
openalex-w4407676845: Scorpion venom hides a blue chemical that kills superbugs. This paper tells how a venom compound was pulled out and tested against drug-proof germs. The team measured its killing power in lab dishes. A nature-drug study of venom turned healer, with hope for new drugs.
pmc-13463745: This 2026 nursing study asked how perceived stress affects work engagement among ICU nurses, and whether dispositional mindfulness — a person's baseline ability to stay present — softens the blow. Based on survey data, the authors map the pathway from stress to disengagement. The results speak to burnout prevention in critical care.
pmc-13459645: This 2026 review surveys research on leeches and their role in treating diabetic ulcer fibrosis — the thick, non-healing scar tissue around diabetic wounds. Leech therapy has ancient roots, but the paper focuses on modern findings about mechanisms and progress. It gathers scattered evidence into one place for clinicians interested in unconventional wound care.
pmc-13451645: This 2026 paper describes developing and pre-testing PREVAIL, a program to help adults with rheumatoid arthritis keep doing the activities they value most. Rather than focusing only on symptoms, the module targets the daily life that arthritis erodes. Patient-centered design like this aims at what sufferers actually care about.
pmc-13447445: This 2026 paper presents a serverless dashboard that translates pharmacogenomic risk models — predictions of how your genes affect drug response — into clinical decision support using ensemble models and scenario rules. Serverless design keeps it cheap and scalable. The tool aims to bring gene-guided prescribing to the bedside.
pmc-13474645: This 2026 environmental engineering paper designs an eco-efficient sonocatalytic process — ultrasound plus catalyst — using iron-modified bamboo biochar to kill cyanobacteria and convert the resulting algal organic matter into something useful. Harmful algal blooms plague water supplies, and this approach both clears and valorizes the waste. Bamboo biochar keeps it cheap and green.
pmc-13450645: This 2026 veterinary ophthalmology paper characterizes a large animal model of RDH5-associated retinopathy, an inherited retinal disease. Large animal models — closer to human eye size and biology than mice — are essential for testing gene therapies. The functional and structural data establish the model for future treatment trials.
pmc-13417745: This 2026 animal reproduction paper found that follicle size regulates cytoplasmic maturation, lipid content, and embryo cryosurvival in cow oocytes matured in vitro. Bigger follicles make hardier eggs for freezing. The finding improves in-vitro embryo production for cattle breeding.
pmc-13472145: A 2026 prospective study on prenatal exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons — pollutants from combustion — combined with maternal genetic susceptibility, and children's growth trajectories. Both environment and genes shaped the outcomes. The evidence strengthens the case for protecting pregnant people from air pollution.
pmc-13578045: A 2026 correction notice for a systematic review and meta-analysis on the accuracy of vestibular schwannoma segmentation using deep learning models. Corrections formally amend the published record. This entry preserves the correction as the journal issued it.
pmc-13461645: A 2026 pediatric oncology paper on watchful waiting in children with unifocal osseous Langerhans cell histiocytosis — a single bone lesion. Sometimes the best treatment is none. The study supports restraint for this presentation.
pmc-13525845: In this 2026 dental stem cell paper, calcium channel subunit alpha2delta2 was upregulated during odontoblast-like differentiation and showed higher basal expression in stem cells from exfoliated deciduous teeth. The channel subunit marks tooth-forming potential. The finding aids regenerative dentistry.
pmc-13422345: A 2026 correction notice for a paper on serum and cerebral folate in Down Syndrome Regression Disorder. Corrections amend the record. This entry preserves the correction.
pmc-13629345: This 2026 data paper presented ADCP-derived current profiles and sea level measurements from Buli Bay, East Halmahera, Indonesia. The oceanographic dataset supports regional marine science. The measurements are the resource.
pmc-13530745: This 2026 conference poster reported clinical outcomes after split anconeus fascia transfer for lateral ulnar collateral reconstruction of the elbow. The surgical technique was evaluated. The poster presents the results.
pmc-13530145: This 2026 AI paper used deep-learning multi-omics analyses to predict future metastasis in cancer. The omics integration forecasted spread. The prediction model is the advance.
pmc-13485345: This 2026 paper addressed neonatal sepsis definitions for randomized trials — challenges and approaches. Defining sepsis in newborns is notoriously hard. The paper proposes solutions.
pmc-13480345: A 2026 paper on shockwave-induced myoblast exosome-like vesicles as emerging drivers of muscle regeneration. The sound waves' vesicles healed muscle. The vesicles are the mechanism.
pmc-13478845: This 2026 cancer paper showed ETS1-EGR2 facilitates renal cell carcinoma progression by activating NOTCH signaling. The transcription factor duo drove the kidney cancer. The NOTCH activation is the mechanism.
pmc-13474245: A 2026 NHANES-based paper on hidden nutritional inadequacy in US children with obesity — evidence from 2021–2023. The overfed but undernourished paradox was quantified. The inadequacy is the public health concern.
pmc-13470445: This 2026 paper used bioinspired nanoparticles to deliver DNase I, attenuating ulcerative colitis by degrading NETs and modulating PTGS2-mediated ER stress. The enzyme-loaded particles calmed the inflamed gut. The delivery is the innovation.
pmc-13466845: This 2026 aquaculture paper tested mulberry leaf extract effects on grass carp growth, organ indices, flesh quality, collagen metabolism, and myofiber development (the title is truncated). The leaf supplement improved the fish. The extract is the feed additive.
pmc-13445145: This 2026 neuroscience paper found a selective cortico-limbic network organized behavior during reward seeking under threat. The brain's risk-reward circuit was mapped. The network is the discovery.

arxiv-2606-15945: A pure mathematics paper in geometric group theory, which studies groups (collections of symmetries) by picturing them as shapes. The result fills a gap in the theory of how abstract groups can grow, and mainly interests specialists in the field.
arxiv-2606-16045: Labeling training data is expensive, so active learning picks only the most useful examples to label. This paper improves the selection using low-rank structure — the idea that the data's important patterns live in a small space. The authors show this guides smarter choices of which examples to label, cutting costs for teams training large models.
arxiv-2606-16145: Primordial black holes — hypothetical black holes born in the early universe — might carry a "memory burden" that changes how they evaporate. This paper uses neutrino observations from dwarf spheroidal galaxies to constrain that idea, putting limits on which memory-burdened black holes can exist. It targets cosmologists and particle astrophysicists.
arxiv-2606-16245: Kagome magnets — materials with a basket-weave atomic pattern — host strange quantum behavior. This paper studies ScFe6Ge6, an antiferromagnet in the FeGe family, tracking how its electron bands evolve for different atomic orbitals and how correlations act between layers. It targets condensed-matter physicists mapping quantum materials.
arxiv-2606-16445: Axions are hypothetical particles that could make up dark matter, and cosmic strings are giant relics of the early universe. This particle-cosmology paper shows how high-quality axion strings can arise from monopole strings — heavier defects decaying into them. It targets theorists connecting dark matter to early-universe physics.
